Example (EN): Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Notes: Also "el sanitario". In Spain often "el servicio" or "el aseo". Doors may say "Damas / Caballeros".

Example (EN): Hi, how are you?
Notes: The h is silent.

Example (EN): Good morning, sir. How are you?
Notes: Used until about noon, then "buenas tardes". "Buen día" is also heard in Mexico.

Example (EN): Good evening, do you have a table for two?
Notes: Used both as a greeting after dark and when saying goodbye.

Example (EN): A coffee, please.
Thank you very much for your help.
"Thanks." "You're welcome."
Notes: Also "por nada". Very common in Mexico: "a sus órdenes" or "para servirle".

Example (EN): Excuse me, do you speak English?
Notes: Formal (usted). Informal: "disculpa". "Perdón" is also common.

English: excuse me (to get past or to leave)
Example (EN): Excuse me, I'm getting off here.
Notes: Said when squeezing past people or leaving a table. Typical Mexican reply: "Propio" or "Adelante".

Example (EN): Nice to meet you, my name is Ana.
Notes: Reply: "Igualmente" or "El gusto es mío".

Example (EN): Excuse me, how much is this T-shirt?
Notes: Plural: "¿Cuánto cuestan?". "¿Cuánto es?" for the total. "La playera" = T-shirt in Mexico (Spain: "la camiseta").

Example (EN): Could you bring us the check, please?
Notes: Waiters usually won't bring it until you ask.

Example (ES): En México se deja de 10 a 15 % de {{c1::propina}}.
Example (EN): In Mexico you leave a 10 to 15% tip.
Notes: Usually not included in the bill. "¿Incluye el servicio?" = Is service included?

Example (EN): Can I pay in cash?
Notes: Many small shops and street stalls only take cash.

Example (EN): Do you take cards?
Notes: "Tarjeta de crédito / de débito".

Example (EN): Where do I pay?
Notes: Preterite: yo pagué (spelling change g → gu).

Example (EN): Keep the change.
Notes: "La casa de cambio" = currency exchange office. Mexican slang for small change: "la feria".

Example (EN): That's one hundred pesos, please.
Notes: "Cien" alone or before a noun; "ciento" in compounds: ciento veinte (120). 500 = quinientos, 1,000 = mil.

Example (EN): This market is very cheap.

Example (ES): La comida en el aeropuerto es muy {{c1::cara}}.
Example (EN): The food at the airport is very expensive.
Notes: Agrees in gender and number: caro, cara, caros, caras.

Example (EN): Where is the subway station?
Notes: Plural: "¿Dónde están…?". "¿Dónde queda…?" is also very common in Mexico.

English: to the right, on the right
Example (EN): The hotel is on the right.

English: to the left, on the left
Example (ES): Dé vuelta {{c1::a la izquierda}} en el semáforo.
Example (EN): Turn left at the traffic light.
Notes: Mexico: "dar vuelta" or "voltear"; Spain: "girar".

Example (EN): Go straight ahead for two blocks.
Notes: Spain prefers "recto". Don't confuse with "a la derecha" (to the right).

Example (EN): The pharmacy is three blocks away.
Notes: Spain: "la manzana".

Example (EN): See you at the corner.
Notes: An inside corner of a room is "el rincón".

Example (EN): We take the bus downtown.
Notes: Everyday Mexican word for a city bus (also means truck). Spain: "el autobús". Plural: los camiones.

Example (ES): El {{c1::metro}} de la Ciudad de México es muy barato.
Example (EN): The Mexico City subway is very cheap.
I need a ticket to Oaxaca.
Notes: Spain: "el billete" (which in Mexico means a banknote).

Example (EN): Which stop do I get off at?
Notes: "Bajarse" = to get off; "subirse" = to get on.

Example (EN): How much is a taxi to the airport?
Notes: "al" = a + el.

Example (EN): I lost my suitcase.
Notes: "El equipaje" = luggage. "La valija" is used in some other countries.

Example (ES): Rentamos un {{c1::carro}} para ir a la playa.
Example (EN): We rented a car to go to the beach.
Notes: Mexico: "carro" or "coche"; Spain: "coche". "Rentar" is Mexican (Spain: "alquilar").

English: Can I have…?, Could you give me…?
Example (ES): ¿{{c1::Me da}} dos tacos al pastor, por favor?
Example (EN): Can I have two al pastor tacos, please?
Notes: Polite standard way to order or buy (usted). Informal: "¿Me das…?".

English: Could I have…? (lit. "will you gift me…?")
Example (EN): Could I have a glass of water?
Notes: Friendly, very common way to ask for something in Mexico; you still pay. Formal: "¿Me regala…?".

Example (EN): A bottle of water, please.
Notes: Feminine but takes "el" (stressed a): el agua fría, las aguas. Tap water: "agua de la llave" (Spain: "del grifo"); drink "agua purificada". "¡Aguas!" = Watch out! (Mexican slang).

Example (EN): Can you bring me the menu?
Notes: "La carta" is also used. A cheap set lunch is "la comida corrida" or "el menú del día".

Example (EN): Is this salsa very spicy?
Notes: Common question: "¿Pica?" (Is it spicy?). Ask for "sin chile" if needed.

Example (EN): Is breakfast included?
Notes: Verb: "desayunar". Dinner: "la cena".

Example (EN): Mexican food is delicious.
Notes: In Mexico also the main afternoon meal (about 2–4 p.m.); in Spain that meal is often "el almuerzo".

Example (EN): Our hotel is near downtown.
Notes: The h is silent.

Example (EN): I'd like a double room.
Notes: "El cuarto" is very common in Mexico.

Example (ES): Tengo una {{c1::reservación}} a nombre de Smith.
Example (EN): I have a reservation under the name Smith.
Notes: Mexico: "reservación"; Spain: "reserva".

Example (EN): Help! Call an ambulance!
Notes: Also "¡Auxilio!". Emergency number in Mexico: 911.

Example (EN): Where is the nearest hospital?
Notes: The h is silent.

Example (EN): There's a pharmacy on the corner.
We need to call the police.
Notes: "La policía" = the police force; "el/la policía" = a police officer.

Example (EN): My friend is sick.
Notes: Use with "estar": estoy enfermo / enferma. "Me siento mal" = I feel sick.

Example (EN): Excuse me, what time is it?
Notes: Answers: "Es la una", "Son las tres".

English: right now, in a little while
Example (EN): I'll be right back.
Notes: Very Mexican and flexible: can mean "right now" or "later, eventually"; context and tone decide.

Example (EN): I practice archery on Saturdays.
Notes: "La arquería" is also heard in Mexico.

Example (EN): The archer aims at the center.
Notes: In soccer "arquero" can mean goalkeeper (Mexico usually says "portero").

Example (ES): La {{c1::arquera}} ganó la medalla de oro.
Example (EN): The archer won the gold medal.
My bow is 30 pounds.
Notes: Also means "arch".

Example (EN): I pulled the arrow out of the target.
Keep the arrows in the quiver.
Notes: Plural: los carcajes. Also "la aljaba".

Example (ES): La {{c1::cuerda}} del arco está muy gastada.
Example (EN): The bowstring is very worn.

Example (ES): El {{c1::emplumado}} estabiliza la flecha en el aire.
Example (EN): The fletching stabilizes the arrow in flight.
Notes: Individual vanes are "las plumas" (feathers) or "las aletas" (plastic vanes). Verb: "emplumar".

Example (ES): La {{c1::punta}} de la flecha se dobló.
Example (EN): The arrow point bent.
Put the nock on the string.
Notes: Also just "el nock" in archery shops. Plural: los culatines.

Example (ES): Ajusta la {{c1::mira}} un poco hacia arriba.
Example (EN): Move the sight up a little.

Example (ES): El {{c1::estabilizador}} reduce la vibración del arco.
Example (EN): The stabilizer reduces the bow's vibration.
I use a leather finger tab.
Notes: Also "el protector de dedos".

Example (ES): Ponte el {{c1::brazal}} para que la cuerda no te pegue.
Example (EN): Put on your arm guard so the string doesn't hit you.
Notes: Also "el protector de antebrazo".

Example (EN): The target face has ten rings.
Notes: In Mexico "el blanco" is also very common.

Example (EN): I hit the target.
Notes: Also the adjective "white". "Dar en el blanco" = to hit the mark.

Example (ES): Las flechas se quedan clavadas en la {{c1::paja}}.
Example (EN): The arrows stick in the straw.
Notes: The target butt is also called "el parapeto" or "la paca"; many ranges use foam ("espuma").

Example (ES): Hoy tiramos a una {{c1::distancia}} de 18 metros.
Example (EN): Today we're shooting at a distance of 18 meters.

Example (ES): Todos detrás de la {{c1::línea de tiro}}.
Example (EN): Everyone behind the shooting line.
Notes: "Tirar" = to shoot (in archery).

Example (EN): My arrow landed in the center.
Notes: The ten ring is "el diez". In a city "el centro" means downtown.

Example (EN): What was your score?
Notes: "El puntaje" is also common in Latin America. "Los puntos" = points.

Example (EN): I advanced to the second round.

Example (ES): Mañana tengo una {{c1::competencia}} de tiro con arco.
Example (EN): Tomorrow I have an archery competition.
Notes: Mexico: "competencia"; Spain: "competición". Also means "the competitors / rivals".

Example (ES): El {{c1::campo de tiro}} abre a las ocho.
Example (EN): The range opens at eight.

Example (ES): El {{c1::arco recurvo}} es el que se usa en los Juegos Olímpicos.
Example (EN): The recurve bow is the one used in the Olympic Games.
The compound bow has cams.
Notes: "Las poleas" = cams / pulleys.

Example (ES): Con el arco compuesto se usa un {{c1::disparador}}.
Example (EN): With a compound bow you use a release aid.

Example (ES): La flecha se apoya en el {{c1::reposaflechas}}.
Example (EN): The arrow sits on the arrow rest.
Notes: Same form in the plural: los reposaflechas. Also "el apoyaflechas".

Example (ES): Las {{c1::palas}} del arco se doblan al tensar.
Example (EN): The bow's limbs bend when you draw.
Notes: Also "las ramas" or "los brazos". Singular "la pala" also means shovel.

Example (EN): Don't squeeze the grip.
Notes: The middle section of the bow is "el cuerpo" or "el riser".

Example (EN): Draw the bow slowly.
Notes: Also "abrir el arco".

Example (EN): Your shoulders are very tense.
Aim at the center of the target.
Notes: Also means "to write down".

Example (EN): Release the string smoothly.
Notes: Stem-changing (o → ue): suelto, sueltas. Noun: "la suelta" = the release.

Example (EN): Wait for the whistle before shooting.
Notes: In archery "tirar" is also very common: "¿A qué distancia tiras?".

Example (ES): {{c1::Ancla}} la mano debajo de la barbilla.
Example (EN): Anchor your hand under your chin.
Always find the same anchor point.
Notes: Also "el punto de anclaje".

Example (EN): A good stance improves accuracy.
Let's go collect the arrows.
Notes: Spelling change: yo recojo. Also "ir por las flechas".

Example (EN): I missed the last shot.

English: to hit (the target), to get right
Example (EN): Today almost all my arrows hit the target.
Notes: Stem-changing (e → ie): acierto, aciertas.

Example (EN): Start with a low draw weight.
Notes: Measured in pounds ("libras"). Also "la potencia del arco".

Example (EN): Stop! There's someone on the range.
Notes: Safety call: everyone stops shooting immediately. Also the word on Mexican stop signs.

Example (ES): ¡{{c1::Cuidado}}! No camines frente a la línea.
Example (EN): Watch out! Don't walk in front of the line.
Notes: Informal Mexican alternative: "¡Aguas!".

Example (ES): La {{c1::seguridad}} es lo más importante en el campo de tiro.
Example (EN): Safety is the most important thing at the range.

Example (ES): Tres toques de {{c1::silbato}}: pueden ir a recoger las flechas.
Example (EN): Three whistle blasts: you may go collect your arrows.
Notes: Usual range signals: 2 = go to the line, 1 = start shooting, 3 = collect arrows, 4 or more = stop immediately.

Example (EN): Each end is six arrows.
Notes: Some ranges say "la serie".

Example (EN): The judge checks the borderline arrows.
Notes: Plural: los jueces. Female: la jueza (or la juez).

Example (ES): Hoy hay mucho {{c1::viento}}; apunta un poco a la izquierda.
Example (EN): It's very windy today; aim a little to the left.
My dominant eye is the right one.

Example (ES): Voy al {{c1::gimnasio}} cuatro veces por semana.
Example (EN): I go to the gym four times a week.
Notes: Colloquial in Mexico: "el gym" (pronounced "yim").

Example (EN): I like lifting weights.
Notes: "Hacer pesas" = to lift weights. Singular: la pesa.

Example (EN): Put more plates on the bar.
Notes: "La barra olímpica" = Olympic barbell. "La barra fija" = pull-up bar.

Example (EN): Use ten-kilo dumbbells.
Notes: Singular: la mancuerna. Also simply called "pesas".

Example (EN): Put the plates away when you're done.
Notes: Singular: el disco.

Example (EN): Set the bench to 30 degrees.
Notes: Also means "bank".

Example (EN): Can I use the rack when you're done?
Notes: English loanword used in Mexican gyms. A power cage is also "la jaula".

Example (ES): Me pongo las {{c1::rodilleras}} para hacer sentadillas.
Example (EN): I put on my knee sleeves to do squats.

Example (ES): Usa el {{c1::cinturón}} en las series pesadas.
Example (EN): Use the belt on heavy sets.
Notes: Plural: los cinturones. In Mexico a support belt is also "la faja".

Example (EN): This machine is for the legs.
Today I'm doing five sets of squats.
Notes: "Sentadilla frontal" = front squat; "sentadilla búlgara" = Bulgarian split squat.

Example (ES): El {{c1::peso muerto}} trabaja toda la espalda.
Example (EN): The deadlift works your whole back.
Notes: Literally "dead weight". "Peso muerto rumano" = Romanian deadlift.

Example (ES): Mi récord en {{c1::press de banca}} es de 80 kilos.
Example (EN): My bench press record is 80 kilos.
Notes: Also "press de pecho" or "press plano".

Example (EN): The overhead press strengthens the shoulders.
I still can't do pull-ups.
Notes: Related Mexican gym term: "jalón al pecho" = lat pulldown (from "jalar", to pull; Spain: "tirar").

Example (ES): Haz el {{c1::remo}} con la espalda recta.
Example (EN): Do the row with a straight back.
Notes: Also means "oar" or "rowing". "Remo con barra" = barbell row.

Example (EN): I did three sets of lunges.
Notes: In Mexico also "los desplantes".

Example (EN): I finish every workout with ab exercises.
Notes: Refers to both the muscles and the exercises.

Example (EN): Do twenty push-ups.
Notes: Mexican usage (literally "little lizards"). Spain: "las flexiones".

Example (EN): I have one more set left.
Notes: Also means "TV series".

Example (EN): Do ten reps per set.
Notes: Colloquial: "las reps".

Example (ES): Toma un {{c1::descanso}} de dos minutos entre series.
Example (EN): Take a two-minute rest between sets.
Your muscles grow when you rest.
How much weight did you put on the bar?
Notes: Also the Mexican currency (el peso mexicano).

Example (EN): This bar is very heavy.
Notes: Said of a person, it means "annoying": "¡Qué pesado!".

Example (EN): Start with a light weight.
Notes: Also "liviano".

Example (ES): {{c1::Levanto}} pesas los lunes, miércoles y viernes.
Example (EN): I lift weights on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.
Notes: "Levantarse" = to get up.

Example (EN): What time do you work out?
Notes: Also "hacer ejercicio".

Example (EN): My trainer corrects my form.
Notes: "Entrenador personal" = personal trainer. Also "el coach".

Example (ES): La {{c1::entrenadora}} nos dio una rutina nueva.
Example (EN): The trainer gave us a new routine.
I always warm up before lifting.
Notes: Stem-changing (e → ie): caliento, calientas.

Example (EN): The warm-up lasts ten minutes.
You should stretch after working out.
Notes: Noun: "el estiramiento" (stretch).

Example (EN): I want to get stronger.
You're very strong.
Notes: Also "loud". Informal Mexican slang for very muscular: "mamado".

Example (EN): This muscle hurts.
Notes: "Ganar músculo" = to build muscle.

Example (EN): Today is back and biceps.
Notes: "Hoy toca…" = today it's time for…

Example (ES): El press de banca trabaja el {{c1::pecho}}.
Example (EN): The bench press works the chest.

Example (ES): Nunca te saltes el día de {{c1::pierna}}.
Example (EN): Never skip leg day.
Notes: Gym talk uses the singular: "día de pierna".

Example (EN): My right shoulder hurts.
Fully extend your arms.
Squats work the glutes.
Notes: Singular: el glúteo.

Example (ES): No dejes que la {{c1::rodilla}} se vaya hacia adentro.
Example (EN): Don't let your knee cave in.
Push your hips back.
Keep your back straight! Don't hunch over.

English: Brace your core!, Tighten your abs!
Example (EN): Before you go down, brace your core!
Notes: "Apretar" is stem-changing (e → ie); "aprieta" is the tú command. Also "¡Activa el core!".

Example (EN): Use a wider grip.
Notes: Verb: "agarrar" (to grab, to take), the everyday verb in Mexico. Avoid Spain's "coger": it is vulgar in Mexico.

Example (ES): Estoy {{c1::adolorido}} por el entrenamiento de ayer.
Example (EN): I'm sore from yesterday's workout.
Notes: Spain: "dolorido", or "tener agujetas" for muscle soreness.

Example (ES): Me tomo un licuado de {{c1::proteína}} después de entrenar.
Example (EN): I have a protein shake after working out.
Notes: Mexico: "el licuado" = shake or smoothie (Spain: "el batido").

Example (EN): I sweated a ton in class.
Notes: Noun: "el sudor".

Example (EN): My cat sleeps all day.
Notes: In Mexico "el gato" is also tic-tac-toe, the # sign, and a car jack.

Example (EN): The cat had four kittens.
Notes: Careful: in Mexico "gata" is also a derogatory slang word for a maid; with cats it's perfectly normal.

Example (EN): The kitten is playing with a ball.
Notes: Diminutive of "gato" (-ito).

Example (EN): We adopted a white kitten.
Look at that cute kitty!
Notes: Very common in Mexico and online; also "michito". To call a cat people say "mish, mish" or "michi, michi".

Example (ES): Nunca le cortes los {{c1::bigotes}} a un gato.
Example (EN): Never cut a cat's whiskers.
Notes: Singular "el bigote" also means mustache.

Example (ES): El gato mueve la {{c1::cola}} cuando está molesto.
Example (EN): The cat swishes its tail when it's annoyed.
Notes: In Spain "la cola" is also a line of people; Mexico usually says "la fila".

Example (EN): The cat put its claws out.
Notes: "Las uñas" (nails) is also common: "cortarle las uñas al gato".

Example (EN): My cat has pink paw pads.
Notes: "La almohada" = pillow. "Las patitas" = little paws.

Example (ES): Tu gata tiene un {{c1::pelaje}} muy suave.
Example (EN): Your cat has very soft fur.
Notes: Everyday word: "el pelo".

Example (ES): El gato echó las {{c1::orejas}} hacia atrás.
Example (EN): The cat flattened its ears back.
Notes: "La oreja" = outer ear; "el oído" = inner ear, hearing.

Example (ES): La {{c1::lengua}} del gato es muy áspera.
Example (EN): A cat's tongue is very rough.
Notes: Also means "language".

Example (EN): My cat purrs when I pet her.

Example (ES): Me encanta el {{c1::ronroneo}} de mi gato.
Example (EN): I love my cat's purring.
The cat is meowing at the door.
Notes: Written accent on the stressed u: maúllo, maúllas, maúlla.

Example (EN): I heard a meow outside.
Notes: The sound itself is written "miau".

Example (EN): The cat scratched the armchair.
Notes: Noun: "el arañazo".

Example (EN): Careful, my cat scratches.
Notes: Very common in Mexico; noun: "el rasguño". For scratching an itch use "rascarse".

Example (ES): La gata {{c1::bufó}} cuando vio al perro.
Example (EN): The cat hissed when she saw the dog.
Notes: Noun: "el bufido".

Example (ES): Los gatos {{c1::se acicalan}} varias horas al día.
Example (EN): Cats groom themselves several hours a day.
Notes: Also "lamerse" or "asearse".

Example (EN): My cat licks my hand.

Example (ES): Los gatos {{c1::duermen}} hasta 16 horas al día.
Example (EN): Cats sleep up to 16 hours a day.
Notes: Stem-changing (o → ue). "Tomar una siesta" = to take a nap.

Example (EN): The kitten jumped onto the table.

Example (ES): A mi gato le gusta {{c1::cazar}} moscas.
Example (EN): My cat likes to hunt flies.
Notes: Spelling change: yo cacé.

Example (ES): El gato {{c1::se esconde}} debajo de la cama.
Example (EN): The cat hides under the bed.
My cat stretches when she wakes up.

Example (ES): Mi gato {{c1::amasa}} la cobija antes de dormir.
Example (EN): My cat kneads the blanket before sleeping.
Notes: Literally "to knead dough"; people also say the cat is "haciendo pan". "La cobija" = blanket (Mexico; Spain: "la manta").

Example (ES): Hay que limpiar el {{c1::arenero}} todos los días.
Example (EN): You have to clean the litter box every day.
Notes: Also "la caja de arena".

Example (EN): I bought cat litter.
Notes: "Arena aglomerante" = clumping litter.

Example (EN): I give him kibble in the morning.
Notes: Mexico: "croquetas"; Spain: "pienso". Wet food: "comida húmeda" or "latas" / "sobres".

Example (ES): Cambia el agua del {{c1::bebedero}} todos los días.
Example (EN): Change the water in the water bowl every day.
Notes: The food bowl is "el plato" or "el comedero".

Example (ES): Le compramos un {{c1::rascador}} para que no arañe los muebles.
Example (EN): We bought him a scratching post so he won't scratch the furniture.
Notes: From "rascar" (to scratch an itch).

Example (EN): I took my cat to the vet.
Notes: Female: "la veterinaria", which also means the vet clinic. Colloquial: "el vete".

Example (ES): Ya le toca su {{c1::vacuna}} contra la rabia.
Example (EN): He's due for his rabies shot.
It's important to spay and neuter cats.
Notes: "Castrar" is also used for males. Many Mexican cities run low-cost "campañas de esterilización".

Example (ES): Hay que {{c1::desparasitar}} al gatito cada tres meses.
Example (EN): You need to deworm the kitten every three months.
Notes: "Los parásitos" = parasites.

Example (EN): My cat has fleas.
Notes: "La pipeta" = spot-on flea treatment.

Example (ES): El {{c1::collar}} tiene una placa con su nombre.
Example (EN): The collar has a tag with his name.
Notes: Also means "necklace".

Example (EN): His favorite toy is a feather.

Example (ES): El gato vomitó una {{c1::bola de pelo}}.
Example (EN): The cat threw up a hairball.
Put the cat in the carrier.
Notes: Mexico: "la transportadora"; Spain: "el transportín".

Example (ES): {{c1::Adoptamos}} a nuestro gato en un refugio.
Example (EN): We adopted our cat from a shelter.
Notes: Popular slogan: "Adopta, no compres" (Adopt, don't shop).

Example (EN): I have a gray tabby cat.
Notes: From "el tigre". Other coats: "carey" (tortoiseshell), "tricolor" (calico), "naranja" (orange).

Example (EN): The kitten is very playful.
Notes: Forms: juguetón, juguetona, juguetones, juguetonas.

Example (EN): My cat is very affectionate.
Fluffy cats shed a lot of hair.

Example (ES): El gato de la calle es un poco {{c1::arisco}}.
Example (EN): The street cat is a little skittish.
Notes: Not aggressive; it just keeps its distance and doesn't like being touched.

Example (ES): Le doy de comer a un gato {{c1::callejero}}.
Example (EN): I feed a stray cat.
Notes: From "la calle" (street).

Example (ES): El gato trajo un {{c1::ratón}} a la casa.
Example (EN): The cat brought a mouse into the house.
Notes: Plural: los ratones. Also a computer mouse.

Example (ES): A mi gata le encanta la {{c1::hierba gatera}}.
Example (EN): My cat loves catnip.
Notes: Many people in Mexico just say "catnip".
